newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia telecom deregulation to spur growth.
newsitem.headline: Australia telecom deregulation to spur growth.

text.p: The full deregulation of Australia's A$25 billion telecommunications industry is to stimulate economic growth, communications minister Richard Alston said on Monday.

"The new world of telecommunications which begins tomorrow will turn the telecommunications industry into a powerful engine of growth and properity for Australia," Alston said in a speech to a seminar held by the Australian Telecommunciations Users Group (ATUG) and the Communications Law Centre.
Under full deregulation of the industry on July 1, an unlimited number of telephone carriers will be allowed.

"It will create new jobs in new industries, it will provide better and cheaper service to small business, to families and to the bush and it will make Australia much more internationally competitive than ever before," Alston said.
Alston said Australia's communictaions sector grew at 12 percent in the year to June 1996 over twice the rate of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP).
He said jobs in the local telecommunications sector have risen by about 20 percent in the past two and a half years to almost 95,000 in February 1997 from 80,000 in August 1994.

Alston said telecommunications is a vital input to virtually every sector of the economy. "With better services and lower prices flowing from competition, the entire Australian economy gets a boost - and more jobs across the board," he said.

Government advisory agency the Industry Commission in a recent report said the average price call from Australia could fall almost 60 percent to 47 cents a minuster from A$1.11 and produce efficiency gains of A$350 million.
He said cheap communications would make Australia a more attractive place in which to invest and locate the Asian regional headquarters of multinational companies.
"I am confident there will be significant employment benefits for Australia from the deregulation," Alston said.

"Every new phone company, or Internet service provider, or online content operator, will need people to install and run their services. That means jobs -- potentially tens of thousands of them," he said.
The minister said he would visit major telecommunications and online service firms in the United States, Japan and Britain later this month to promote Australian as a place in which to invest.
"Attracting foreign investment into Australia will not only ensure Australian have access to the latest technologies, but will also create new jobs in exciting new industries," Alston said.
